exploration.title: Bridge Builder
exploration.subject: Engineering
exploration.summary: Move one static point load and compare support reactions, bending moment and modeled beam deflection.
exploration.question: How do load position and load size change the forces and bending of a simply supported beam?
exploration.explanation: Static equilibrium requires the upward support reactions to equal the downward point load and their torques to balance. Moving the load changes how the two supports share it. This activity also calculates peak bending moment and small deflection for a 10 m equivalent beam with a fixed flexural rigidity EI. The timber truss is explanatory artwork, not the structure being solved. Brace buttons change only an invented comparison index; they do not calculate truss forces, member capacity or a safe load.

experiments.title: Move the same load
experiments.instruction: Keep the 10 m span, 12 kN point load, 100 MN·m² flexural rigidity and brace index fixed. Predict which support carries more when the load moves from the center to 20% of the span, then compare both trials.
experiments.observe: At the center, both reactions are 6.0 kN. At 20%, the left reaction is 9.6 kN and the right is 2.4 kN; peak moment and deflection at the load are also smaller. Explain how force and torque balance support this result.

experiments.title: Double the point load
experiments.instruction: Keep the load at midspan, the 10 m span, 100 MN·m² flexural rigidity and brace index fixed. Predict what happens to peak moment and deflection when the point load changes from 8 to 16 kN, then compare.
experiments.observe: Peak moment changes from 20.0 to 40.0 kN·m and deflection at the load changes from 1.67 to 3.33 mm. Explain why both double in this linear beam model and why that does not identify a safe load.

exploration.misconception: A triangular frame or a low teaching index does not prove that a bridge is safe. Real design also checks member forces, connections, shear, buckling, fatigue, impact, wind, material limits, safety factors and other loads.
